title: Exact free induction for forgetting a commuting profinite action
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring on the small coherent profinite site in a universe containing all parameter sets [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention]. Use internal $R$-modules $\mathcal M_R$ [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and action categories $\mathcal A_P(R)$ for the condensed group $\underline P(S)=C(S,P)$ [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Let $G$ be profinite and $J$ be either a profinite group or $\mathbf Z_{\mathrm{disc}}$. All of $\mathcal A_G(R)$, $\mathcal A_J(R)$ and $\mathcal A_{G\times J}(R)$ are Grothendieck abelian and have enough injectives. Their kernels are underlying kernels and their cokernels are underlying sheafified cokernels. Trivial-$J$ inflation $L_J^G$ is exact and has as right adjoint the submodule $\Gamma_J^G$ of sections fixed by $J$ after every profinite base change. The adjunction transpose restricts the codomain to this submodule and its inverse composes with its inclusion.

Forgetting $G$, written $U_J:\mathcal A_{G\times J}(R)\to\mathcal A_J(R)$ and $U_0:\mathcal A_G(R)\to\mathcal M_R$, is exact and conservative both on modules and on the full ordinary unbounded derived categories. There are exact left adjoints
$$F_{G,J}(M)=R[\underline G]\otimes_R M\dashv U_J,\qquad F_{G,1}\dashv U_0,$$
where $G$ translates the free generators and $J$ acts on $M$. The adjunction sends $f:M\to U_JN$ to $[g]\otimes m\mapsto g f(m)$; its inverse evaluates at $[1]\otimes m$. The free module is canonically $R[\underline G]=j_{G!}R_G$ for the representable profinite test object $G$ and is flat. In particular $U_J,U_0$ preserve injective objects and bounded-below injective resolutions. These assertions include $G=1$, $J=1$ and the zero ring.

proof.text: Pass between internal modules and sectionwise module sheaves using [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. This leaves sections, restriction maps and equivariance equations unchanged. For $P=G,J,G\times J$, compatible continuous maps $S_i\to P$ on a finite jointly surjective profinite cover descend to a unique set map $S\to P$: agreement on $S_i\times_S S_j$ makes it well-defined. The surjection $\coprod_iS_i\to S$ is closed, since its source is compact and $S$ is Hausdorff, hence quotient; the descended map is continuous. Thus $\underline P$ is a group sheaf, including discrete $J=\mathbf Z$. Apply [lem-sfb-sheaf-action-grothendieck-inflation] to $P=G,J,G\times J,1$. It supplies the asserted Grothendieck abelian structures, underlying kernels and sheafified cokernels, exact restriction of actions, and detection of zero objects. Apply [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives] to obtain enough injectives.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written categorical expansion: action sheaves and abelian infrastructure

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-sheaf-product-fixed-adjunction] to the group sheaves $\underline G,\underline J$, noting $\underline{G\times J}=\underline G\times\underline J$ by the continuous-map product property. This gives $L_J^G\dashv\Gamma_J^G$ with exactly the base-change fixed-section condition and the two stated transpose formulas. Inflation is exact by [lem-sfb-sheaf-action-grothendieck-inflation] applied to the first projection. For $U_J$, instead restrict along $J\to G\times J$, $j\mapsto(1,j)$; for $U_0$, restrict along $1\to G$. These functors are exact. If $f:M\to N$ becomes invertible after restriction, let $v$ be its inverse, regarded as a module map. For every test object $S$ and parameter $p\in P(S)$, equivariance gives $f_Sa_p=b_pf_S$, hence $a_pv_S=v_Sb_p$. Thus $v$ commutes with the full $P$-action, not just the retained subgroup; its restriction compatibility and linearity already hold because it is a module map. It is therefore an inverse in the original action category, proving conservativity of both restrictions.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written expansion: normalized product invariants and restriction of actions

proof.text: Let $P_G(S)=\bigoplus_{g\in C(S,G)}R(S)$ with restriction carrying $[g]$ to $[g|_T]$. Its sheafification is $R[\underline G]$: a restriction-natural linear map $P_G\to N$ is uniquely specified by the restriction-natural generator map $\underline G\to U_RN$, and factors uniquely through sheafification. This is precisely the free universal property of [def-sfb-condensed-free-module-adjunction]. By [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf] the same presheaf is the extension of $R_G$ from the slice at $G$. Hence $R[\underline G]=j_{G!}R_G$ canonically, with the generator maps identified. Apply [lem-pc-sites-modules-j-shriek-flat] to the object $G$ and ring sheaf $R$ to conclude flatness. This uses representability of $G$, and does not treat $\mathbf Z_{\mathrm{disc}}$ as a profinite test object.

source.place: Tags 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero), 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), 03EV (lemma-j-shriek-flat), applied to the represented object G

proof.text: For $M\in\mathcal A_J(R)$ define the presheaf $Q_M(S)=\bigoplus_{g\in C(S,G)}M(S)$. The tensor/sheafification comparison [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-tensor] identifies $Q_M^\#$ with $R[\underline G]\otimes_RM$, by the maps $r[g]\otimes m\mapsto rm$ in summand $g$ and $m$ in summand $g\mapsto[g]\otimes m$. The relation $(rs)[g]\otimes m=r[g]\otimes sm$ has the same image $rsm$, so the first map is balanced. The composites are identities on each summand and each pure tensor, and restrictions carry both formulas to the same formulas over the restricted section ring. In internal modules the same identification follows directly from the balanced universal property: both sides parametrize restriction-natural families of $R(S)$-linear maps $M(S)\to N(S)$ indexed by $g$, using [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] and the sheaf tensor definition. Define $(a,j)([g]\otimes m)=[ag]\otimes jm$ on every $S$. These operations commute with restrictions and extend uniquely over sheafification; $a(b g)=(ab)g$ and $j(km)=(jk)m$ check the action laws, and the two factors commute. To define the operation on a sheafified section, lift it on a cover, apply the restricted parameter there, and glue; uniqueness follows from local equality. Thus this is a genuine internal action, including nonconstant local parameters. On morphisms use $[g]\otimes m\mapsto[g]\otimes h(m)$; identity and composition hold on these generators.

source.place: Tag 0GMW (lemma-sheafification-tensor), Section 03EK balanced tensor universal property; agent-written commuting action formula

proof.text: For a $J$-equivariant map $f:M\to U_JN$, the maps $[g]\otimes m\mapsto g f(m)$ define a restriction-natural linear map from $Q_M$ and hence a unique map from its sheafification. It is $G$-equivariant since $a(g f(m))=(ag)f(m)$, and $J$-equivariant since $g f(jm)=g j f(m)=j g f(m)$; the middle commutation is the product-action law in $N$. Conversely a $G\times J$-equivariant map $h$ gives $m\mapsto h([1]\otimes m)$, which is $J$-equivariant. The first composite is $1 f(m)=f(m)$; the second is $g h([1]\otimes m)=h([g]\otimes m)$ and therefore equals $h$ on the sheafification. For a $J$-map $u:M'\to M$ and product-action map $v:N\to N'$, both transposing $vfu$ and composing the transpose of $f$ with $F_{G,J}(u)$ and $v$ send $[g]\otimes m$ to $g\,v(f(u(m)))$, since $v$ is $G$-equivariant. Equality extends by sheafification. This proves naturality in both arguments, giving the stated adjunction. Setting $J=1$ gives $F_{G,1}\dashv U_0$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written exact induction expansion: generator/evaluation adjunction

proof.text: The underlying module functor of $F_{G,J}$ is tensoring with the flat module of step 3, hence is exact by [lem-pc-sites-modules-j-shriek-flat]. The forgetful functors from both action categories detect exactness by [lem-sfb-sheaf-action-grothendieck-inflation]. Therefore $F_{G,J}$ is exact, and likewise $F_{G,1}$. Apply [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives] with the exact left adjoint $F_{G,J}:\mathcal A_J(R)\to\mathcal A_{G\times J}(R)$ and right adjoint $U_J$, then with $F_{G,1}:\mathcal M_R\to\mathcal A_G(R)$ and right adjoint $U_0$. These right adjoints preserve injectives in precisely the directions required. Applying an exact functor termwise preserves the exact augmentation and the lower degree bound of any bounded-below injective resolution; every resulting term is injective, so the result is again such a resolution.

Use [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] for each exact restriction $U$ to obtain its triangulated functor on the full ordinary unbounded derived categories, computed termwise. Since $U$ preserves kernels and cokernels, $H^n(UK)=U(H^nK)$ naturally: write $H^n$ as the cokernel of the factorization of $d^{n-1}$ through $\ker d^n$. The comparison is natural on complexes. For an inverted quasi-isomorphism $s$ its naturality square remains commutative after taking inverses of $H^n(s)$ and $U(H^n(s))$; composing these squares gives naturality for every localization morphism, including roofs. Thus it compares the cohomology of $D(U)(f)$ with $U(H^n f)$ for every derived morphism $f$. If $D(U)(f)$ is invertible, all $U(H^n f)$ are invertible. Module-level conservativity from step 2 makes every $H^n f$ invertible. By [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology], $f$ is invertible. This proves derived conservativity without any boundedness assumption. For $G=1$ the generator module is $R$ and induction is the identity; $J=1$ was already used above. For the zero ring every module is zero, and every formula and assertion remains valid.
